build: Two Mastertronic G64 disk variants, with disk IDs AD and TO

exclude: 7 parts: Level resource L1, Level resource L0, Level resource L3 and others
elsewhere: 7 parts: Level resource L1, Level resource L0, Level resource L3 and others

comments.text: Start of the staging image copied to $0393 before TO requests a disk file. $19A9 exchanges all 1,080 bytes with the low memory, then exchanges them back after the call.
The instructions from here become executable at $0417. They prepare the serial handler and hardware state after the drive program has been sent.
Relocates to $047E. Two immediate loads set up the input buffer address and are patched from the chosen file's destination words.
Relocates to $059E. This storage separates the fallback jump into the KERNAL from the drive data at $069E.
Relocates to $069E. The serial setup points at this body and sends it in blocks of 30 bytes to the drive.
Relocates to $06E9. The receiver preparation copies bytes beginning at that address as it iterates eight-bit Y. The part of that source within the exchanged image begins here.

Receives the disk resource selector in A and saves it on the stack. Disables VIC raster interrupts and CIA 1 timer A, installs the loader-time vectors, exposes the KERNAL while keeping I/O active, clears the SID register range and colour RAM, then jumps to the TO-specific transition code at $8100.
Exchanges four pages and another $38 bytes at $1520 with the same span at $0393, using zero-page pointers $02/$04. A second exchange restores the original contents of those spans.

Pops the selector, doubles it, reads the corresponding destination word from $1A16 and the two-character name from $1A2A, then calls SETLFS and SETNAM for drive 8. Calls the low-RAM routine at $0393 before exchanging those bytes back.
Table of ten little-endian destination addresses. The loader copies the selected word into the immediate operands at $047F and $0483 before the low-memory call.
The high byte of each destination word, indexed by twice the selected resource number. The low bytes begin at $1A16.
Consecutive two-byte names L0 through L5, IN, CM, MN and ED. The two bytes after these ten entries are a separate filename buffer, filled by the loader at $1A3E.
Second letters of the two-character resource names, read on the same doubled index as the first letters.
First byte of the selected filename. SETNAM is passed this address and a length of two.
Second byte of the active filename. The remaining bytes before the title are zero padding.

Peeks at the loader selector on the stack. For selector 6 it disables sprites, selects the display through $DD00 and $D018 and writes nine screen codes and their colour cells for GAME OVER before waiting; other selectors go straight to exchanging and loading.
Nine C64 screen codes for GAME OVER, copied to the screen by the TO routine at $811D.
